newsitem.title: USA: Clinton laments lack of golf with Chretien.
newsitem.headline: Clinton laments lack of golf with Chretien.

text.p: President Bill Clinton complained on Tuesday that his bum knee was impeding U.S. relations with Canada because it kept him from golfing with visiting Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien.
"The biggest threat to our friendship is this injury of mine because it has precluded us from indulging our mutual passion for golf," Clinton said at a joint news conference with Chretien.

Clinton, on crutches and forced to endure a layoff from his favourite pastime after knee surgery due to a stumble at the Florida home of golf pro Greg Norman on March 14, hit the links with Chretien after the Halifax economic summit in 1995.
"I don't know if any two world leaders have played golf together more than we have, but we meant to break a record and I've had to take a six-month respite," Clinton said.
Even though the U.S. president has a handicap that has nothing to do with his golf score, Chretien told reporters: "He's a good guy, and I enjoy to be with him."

Chretien, on a reciprocal visit to Washington after Clinton visited Ottawa two years ago, was given rare treatment for a foreign visitor even without golf -- Clinton had him over for a glass of cognac and a private chat on Monday night ahead of Tuesday's colourful White House arrival ceremony and bilateral discussion.
